objective: Optimize the two batch-2 candidates (EOM_REVERSAL_SPY, FRONT_RUN_SECTOR_TOP2) the owner explicitly liked on 2026-09-28, via a bounded, source-grounded parameter variant search per family plus 2 combination variants, judged against a literal preregistered per-family replacement rule.

sources.credibility: author's own job-market-paper PDF (Giuliano Graziani, Bocconi), hosted on his university's own site; abstract also listed on SSRN (papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4349253)
sources.core_claim: Defines the end-of-month reversal signal as the S&P 500 return from the 4th Friday's close to month-end close; the simple rule-of-thumb TSR strategy outperforms buy-and-hold over 45 years. Own robustness appendix (A.1.4) finds only the last week's return (not 2-3 weeks earlier) has predictive power. Section 2.4's magnitude/precision-scaled TSR-TV variant reports Sharpe 0.588 vs simple TSR's 0.384. Replicates on DOW (holds) and Russell 2000 (does not); QQQ not tested.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds E0 (base) and, per its own robustness appendices, E1/E2 (formation window -- source argues against widening it) and E7 (magnitude scaling, modeled on its own best-reported TSR-TV refinement). E3 (threshold), E4 (QQQ), E5/E6 (holding truncation) are owner/brief-directed extensions beyond what the source itself tests.
sources.reflection: Primary source read directly (batch-2 only read a secondary summary). Overfit risk for E1-E7: each changes exactly one dimension from E0, preregistered before any backtest; decay risk untested by this source past its own 2019/2023 sample ends; cost sensitivity: source's own breakeven cost (~16bp/txn) comfortably exceeds this round's 10/20bp convention, so cost alone should not decide most E-family verdicts.

sources.credibility: secondary newsletter summary of Graziani (2024, SSRN); same source batch-2 cited, re-fetched and freshly snapshotted here since batch-2's own dossier never actually saved a copy
sources.core_claim: S&P 500 end-of-month returns (4th Friday to month-end) are negatively correlated with next month's return, in- and out-of-sample; attributed to pension-fund payment-cycle liquidity trading.
sources.project_applicability: Corroborates E0's exact rule, independently of the primary PDF read in this round.
sources.reflection: Secondary source, no quantified numbers of its own; overfit/decay/cost not separately assessable from this source alone.

sources.credibility: Quantpedia's own published strategy page, live-fetched (batch-2 only cited an earlier harvest's summary of an archived snapshot, not a fresh open)
sources.core_claim: Tests holding 1-7 of 9 Select Sector SPDRs, front-running (1-month) shift vs true-seasonality (0-month) shift; top-2 front-running reported best, true-seasonality reported 'at best, comparable to' benchmark. No 2-month shift, multi-year averaging, inverse-vol weighting, or 11-sector universe tested.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds S0 (base) and S1/S2 (top-1/top-3, both source-tested) and S_SHIFT0 (the source's own reported-failing baseline). S_AVG3/S_AVG5/S_SHIFT2/S_11SECTORS/S_INVVOL/S_ABSFILTER are owner/brief-directed extensions.
sources.reflection: Overfit risk for the 9 S-family variants: each changes one dimension from S0, preregistered before any backtest, and the replacement rule's select+2026-guard+20bp conditions are the anti-overfit control since the source's own numeric tables are chart images (not independently re-verifiable from text alone). Decay/cost: see the negative-evidence source below.

sources.credibility: independent third-party (Allocate Smartly) extended backtest of the closely-related country-ETF front-running-seasonality mechanism, no financial interest in the sector-SPDR result
sources.core_claim: Extending the same front-running-seasonality mechanism (applied to 23 country ETFs, not the 9 sector SPDRs) back to 1971 finds it 'would not have been consistently effective over the long-term'; Allocate Smartly stopped tracking it. The sector-SPDR version itself was only on their to-do list, not completed.
sources.project_applicability: Negative-evidence caution motivating this round's conservative replacement rule (select+2026-guard+20bp, not just a raw select-window improvement) for the whole S family.
sources.reflection: Different universe/data than S0-S9; not a direct refutation, but the closest independent replication attempt found for this mechanism family, and the reason this round does not treat any S-family select-window win as sufficient on its own.

sources.reflection: Not independently re-read in full (same underlying paper as the csef.it PDF already read directly); cited for provenance, not as a separate empirical source.

sources.credibility: the paper's own SSRN abstract/landing page, the venue this round's direction-review.json and the registry's dir:end_of_month_reversal_effect entry both reference as the primary citation

sources.project_applicability: Confirms the SSRN identity of the paper already read directly via its csef.it-hosted PDF; grounds the registry citation format.

sources.credibility: independent third-party (Allocate Smartly) extended backtest of the original front-running-seasonality mechanism applied to commodities (Quantpedia's earlier version of the same shift idea, which the sector-SPDR page explicitly says it was modeled on)
sources.core_claim: Allocate Smartly's extended-history test of front-running commodity seasonality found the seasonality-based cut failed out-of-sample when extended, while (counterintuitively) a related momentum cut held up -- 'we expected the seasonality strategy to fail... we were proven wrong; the opposite was true' for one sub-test, but a different momentum-flavored variant (their Test #4) 'failed in our out-of-sample test' after 'working over the specific period tested by the author.'
sources.project_applicability: Second, independent negative-evidence data point (alongside the country-ETF test) for the front-running-seasonality mechanism family generally, reinforcing this round's conservative S-family replacement rule.
sources.reflection: Commodities, not equities/sectors; directional caution only, not a direct test of S0-S9's actual universe.
